text: May 6th is inextricably linked with our respect and gratitude to the invincible Bulgarian military, said Patriarch Daniil (06.05.2026 10:54)

In the tradition of Bulgarian statehood and the Church, May 6 is inextricably linked with our reverence and gratitude toward the invincible Bulgarian military. This was stated by the Bulgarian Patriarch and Metropolitan of Sofia, Daniil, who today led the solemn water blessing and consecration of the battle flags in the capital.

"In unwavering testimony to the triumph of life, which came with the Resurrection of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, I whole-heartedly congratulate you on the most bright feast of the holy and glorious Great Martyr George – a warrior of Christ, wondrous in faith and virtues, and our universally glorified heavenly intercessor and wonderworker. Following the tradition of May 6, on the feast day of Saint George the Victorious, our holy Orthodox Church consecrates the banners of military glory of our victorious Army, imploring God's mercy and protection for our Orthodox host, which preserves the peace and security of our dear homeland and, with a sense of duty, watches over the lives and honor of Bulgarian citizens," Patriarch Daniil added.

In his words, "our prayers and the sacred rites ordained for today's festive day have their foundation in the historically attested truth that always, in our centuries-old Orthodox tradition, the reliance of the Bulgarian military has been first and foremost in God – in Him, from Whom we know that every actual strength and power comes, as well as in our faith in Christ the Savior, which has been a leading conviction not only for Christ's warrior and martyr Saint George, celebrated today by the Holy Church, but also for all Bulgarian warriors who entered battle in defense of their brothers and sisters in faith and kin."

"The sources for the millennial history of our people tell that the tradition of consecrating battle flags dates back to the First Bulgarian Kingdom, from the time of the glorious Bulgarian Tsar Simeon I the Great. The first such historically documented event is the consecration performed in 917 – before the battle at the Achelous River, victorious for Bulgarian arms. In the performance of this ritual, the power of our great ancestors' trust in God and His eternal righteousness is revealed to us; their confidence that without God and the gracious power coming from Him to humans, we can do nothing that is truly good and useful. Our Lord Jesus Christ tells us the same: '...he who abides in Me, and I in him, bears much fruit; for without Me you can do nothing,' Patriarch Daniil reminded."

“Guided by this faith and this conviction, our great ancestors of all times have sought and implored God's help in every endeavor of theirs. This is what we do today as well, when in unity and like-mindedness of Church and state we pray for God's help for our glorious host, peace, light, and prosperity for our people and Motherland. Let the sprinkling of these battle flags with water sanctified through God's grace be yet another testimony of our faith in God and a visible sign of God's favor and God's protection for our entire people and especially for the Bulgarian servicemen who have dedicated their lives to sacrificial military service in the ranks of the Bulgarian Army,” said the Bulgarian Patriarch.
